newsitem.title: USA: TRANSOCEAN OFFSHORE SEES RATES IMPROVING.
newsitem.headline: TRANSOCEAN OFFSHORE SEES RATES IMPROVING.

text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc expects dayrates for offshore rigs to continue to improve and said in a statement with second quarter earnings that it had completed upgrades on all its rigs but one.

"Deepwater drilling programs continue to be a growing component of operators' exploration and development programs and this should place even greater demand on the world's limited supply of deepwater rigs," said J. Michael Talbert, Transocean's chairman.
Net income was $27.9 million, or $0.55 per share, in the second quarter, compared with $21.2 million, $0.74 a year ago.
Including a one-time gain of $4.3 million from a rig sale, the year ago net income was $25.5 million or $0.89 per share.
Analysts had been looking for earnings per share of $0.55 in the second qaurter of 1997.
Transocean said that utilization of the active fleet was 92 percent during the second quarter of 1997, reflecting idle time on rigs in shipyards for extensive upgrading and required surveys.
"This resulted in 200 days at zero rate and the financial results for the period reflect this idle time. All but one of these projects are now complete and the rigs are on contract," said Talbert.
The upgrade for the Transocean Leader rig to 4,500 foot water depth capability will be completed later this month, the company said.
Transocean said that it had recently taken an option to acquire a large tanker which it said is suited for conversion to a deepwater rig in anticipation of higher dayrates.
